cognate: Gk γλυκύς ~ Lat. dulcis (*dl̥k-ú-, Gk with dissimilation/assimilation d->g) and Gk μέλι, μέλιτος ~ Lat. mel, mellis (*mélit-): both slots cognate.
drift_or_renewal: Greek and Latin keep *dl̥kú- + *mélit; Vedic renews both slots (svādú-/svā́dīyas- < *sweh2du-, cognate with Gk ἡδύς; mádhu- < *medhu-, cognate with Gk μέθυ 'wine') but keeps the same comparative figure 'sweeter than honey' and its polyptotic variant 'sweeter than the sweet'.
shared_syntax: Comparative of *dl̥kú- governing the noun *mélit- in the case of comparison: Gk γλυκίων μέλιτος (genitive) = Lat. melle ... dulcior (ablative); plus the attributive epithet+noun 'sweet honey' (Hom. μέλι γλυκερόν, Eur. γλυκεῖαι μέλιτος ῥοαί; Lat. dulce mel, Lucr. dulci melle, mellis dulci liquore). Plautus combines both and adds polyptoton (dulci dulcior), as do the Vedic svādóḥ svā́dīyaḥ and madhoḥ ... madhutaraḥ.
context: The Greek anchors are Aristotle quoting Il. 18.109 (thumos/anger 'much sweeter than dripping honey'), a Homeric formula that recurs at Il. 1.249 in the same metrical slot for Nestor's voice ('from his tongue flowed speech sweeter than honey'). Latin: Plautus Asin. 614, a lover's endearment ('o sweeter than sweet honey'); Lucretius 1.938/947 the honey on the cup's rim, made the figure of his own poetry ('to touch it with the Muses' sweet honey'), i.e. honey for poetic speech. Vedic: RV 8.24.20 and 1.114.6 apply 'sweeter than ghee and honey / sweeter than the sweet' to the poet's speech (vácas), and AVŚ 1.34.4 'I am sweeter than honey' is a love charm, matching the Plautine erotic use. Why not chance: the honey comparison is near-universal (cf. Psalm 19), so the bare idea is not diagnostic; what is diagnostic is (a) the exact Graeco-Latin cognate pair in the identical comparative construction, (b) the shared application to speech/poetry in Greek, Latin and Vedic, and (c) the polyptotic intensification in Latin and Vedic. The Greek-Latin agreement could still be independent use of the ordinary words for 'sweet' and 'honey'; the Vedic match is thematic, with both lexemes renewed.
phrase: *dl̥kú- + *mélit-: 'sweeter than honey' (Gk γλυκίων μέλιτος ~ Lat. melle dulcior), of speech/poetry and of endearment; Vedic renewal vácaḥ ... svā́dīyaḥ mádhunaḥ

cognate: μήτηρ ~ mātā (*méh2tēr), πατήρ ~ pitā (*ph2tḗr) in the same predicative frame; the two divine slots are renewed in the Greek.
drift_or_renewal: Earth: Gk γῆ for Ved. pṛthivī/bhūmi (renewal); Father: Gk ἥλιος 'sun' (and αἰθήρ in Lucretius' Pater aether, Οὐρανός in Hesiod) for Ved. dyaúḥ 'sky', with parjanya 'rain(-god)' in AVŚ 12.1.12 (cf. Lucretius' rain falling from Father Aether into Mother Earth's lap).
shared_syntax: Nominal predication assigning kinship terms to cosmic entities, with the plants as the genitive offspring: Gk ἡ γῆ μήτηρ ... τῶν φυτῶν ὁ δὲ ἥλιος πατήρ ~ Ved. yā́sāṃ (vīrúdhām) dyaúḥ pitā́ pṛthivī́ mātā́ 'of which (plants) Sky is father, Earth mother'; mother/father coordinated as a pair.
context: Both contexts are about the parentage of plants: the AV verses (3.23.6, 8.7.2) praise the healing plants 'whose father is Sky, whose mother is Earth'; the Greek reports Anaxagoras' saying that earth is mother of plants and the sun their father; AVŚ 12.1.12 extends it to the speaker (Earth mother, Parjanya father). The Sky-father / Earth-mother pair itself is directly attested in Vedic (RV 1.191.6, 6.51.5) and, with renewals, in Greek (Hes. Th. 45 Gaia and Ouranos as parents) and Latin (Lucr. 1.250, 2.991, where Father Aether's rain makes Mother Earth bear crops and trees). Caveat on the anchor: the Greek De plantis is a medieval retroversion (Latin < Arabic < Nicolaus of Damascus), so its wording is not ancient Greek phraseology; it witnesses only the Anaxagorean content. The Greek phraseological side therefore rests on support witnesses (Hesiod, Euripides), and the Lucretian passages may draw on Greek models (Euripides' Chrysippus), so they are not independent of Greek. Confidence low for that reason.
phrase: 'Sky/Sun is father, Earth is mother (of the plants)': Ved. dyaúḥ pitā́ pṛthivī́ mātā́ (vīrúdhām) ~ Gk ἡ γῆ μήτηρ ... ὁ δὲ ἥλιος πατήρ (τῶν φυτῶν)

note: Slab dominated by Greek technical prose pivots (Autolycus, Aristotle, ps.-Aristotle De plantis) with Cato/AV/Old Russian partners; nearly all bundles empty. Two claims: 'sweeter than honey' (Gk γλυκίων μέλιτος ~ Lat. melle dulcior, Vedic renewal) medium; Earth-mother / Sky(Sun)-father of plants (De plantis Anaxagoras ~ AVŚ 3.23.6, 8.7.2) low, Greek anchor a medieval retroversion. Rejected: waking/sleeping merism (ἐγρηγορ-/ὑπν- ~ jāgrat/svapant; no Greek formula found), wind blows (generic), honour+gifts (ORU calque risk).
